Just look at Prop 8 in California, which was very close to that hypothetical 51-49 split. It passed by a margin so thin that it wasn't even statistically significant. You might be fine with that, but imagine how you'd feel if it happened to you and something you cared about.

I don't think anything should ever go to a popular referendum that involves restricting individuals or taking away their rights. Rather, I'd like to see it utilized in the opposite direction. Should existing laws (drug prohibition etc) be repealed? They need to be used in such a way that still protects the rights of a minority from the tyranny of a majority, but there a lot of potential referendums that would fall into that category.

Once you start leaving big issues up to referendums, it's inevitable that they will be used to trample on the rights of the minority.

Civil rights and civil liberties never do well at the ballot box. That's why nearly every victory for minority rights has come from constitutional amendments, Supreme Court decisions or legislation.

It is important to remember the US is not a 'democracy' but rather a 'constitutional republic'. That means that while the majority has a say, they don't get to impede or overrule the constitutional rights of the minority. Or, at least, that's the way its supposed to work.
